newsitem.title: DENMARK: Greenland home rule crisis ends after resignation.
newsitem.headline: Greenland home rule crisis ends after resignation.

text.p: A political crisis which split Greenland's two-year-old left-right home rule coalition ended on Sunday after the parliamentary speaker quit, Danish Radio news reported.
"The coalition will hold now that the speaker has resigned," the Arctic territory's Prime Minister Lars Emil Johansen said in a radio interview.
Johansen had said earlier he would start talks on forming a new Greenland government on Monday after a row within his coalition over the competence of the right-wing speaker, Knud Soerensen.
After the last home rule elections in Greenland in March 1995, Johansen's centre-left Siumut party formed a coalition with the main right-wing Atassut grouping for a four-year term in office.
The two parties controlled 22 seats in the 31-seat home rule assembly in Nuuk, the island capital.
But the coalition almost broke apart when Siumut claimed that Soerensen of Atassut was incompetent and demanded his resignation.

"We want to maintain our cooperation with Atassut but we demand that Knud Soerensen resign for his lack of competence in preparing the spring opening of parliament," Johansen earlier told the Danish Ritzau news agency.
The start of the spring session of Greenland's parliament was suspended last Tuesday and postponed until May 2 because of the row.
Atassut said it might try to form a new coalition with the far left pro-independence Inuit Ataqatigiit (IA) grouping, which has six seats in the legislature.
But Soerensen finally agreed on Sunday to go, ensuring that the left-right coalition continued in power.
Danish Radio said he was expected to be replaced as speaker by Siumut's Jonathan Motzfeldt, Greenland's prime minister from 1979-91.
Icebound Greenland, the world's largest island, was colonised by Denmark in 1721 but has had home rule under the Danish crown since 1979.
Denmark controls its foreign and defence policies and provides annual aid of three billion crowns ($460 million), 60 percent of the home rule government's revenue.
